issue.title: Replace EOL debian:jessie with a supported image in VS tests

failure.body:
## Problem

The VS test framework in `tests/conftest.py` (line 397) uses `debian:jessie` as the server container image for simulating network hosts connected to the virtual switch:

```python
self.ctn_sw = self.client.containers.run(cr_prefix + "debian:jessie", ...)
```

**Debian Jessie (Debian 8) has been End-of-Life since June 2018** and no longer receives security updates. Using it introduces security vulnerabilities and dependency risks in the CI pipeline.

## Impact

- The `vstest` job in `azure-pipelines.yml` pulls `publicmirror.azurecr.io/debian:jessie` for every test run.
- The image is used to create virtual server containers that simulate hosts connected to the VS switch.
- EOL images may not be available in all registries and could be removed at any time.

## Proposed Fix

Replace `debian:jessie` with a currently supported Debian image (e.g., `debian:bookworm` or `debian:bullseye`) in `tests/conftest.py`.

The server container is used as a minimal container running `bash`; any modern Debian image should be compatible.

## References

- `tests/conftest.py` line 397
- `.azure-pipelines/test-docker-sonic-vs-template.yml` line 180 (`DEFAULT_CONTAINER_REGISTRY=publicmirror.azurecr.io/`)
- [Debian LTS info](https://wiki.debian.org/LTS)

resolution.title: [tests]: Replace EOL debian:jessie with debian:bookworm in VS tests
resolution.description:
**What I did**

Replaced the EOL `debian:jessie` image with `debian:bookworm` in the VS test framework.
Also removed the now-obsolete Jessie-specific `skipif` decorators in `test_mirror.py` and the unused `distro`/`StrictVersion` imports.

**Why I did it**

`debian:jessie` (Debian 8) has been End-of-Life since June 2018 and no longer receives security updates. The image is pulled on every `vstest` CI run as the server container that provides the network namespace for the virtual switch. Replacing it with a supported image removes the security risk and ensures the image remains available in container registries.

The server container only needs to run `bash` to provide a network namespace — any modern Debian image is a drop-in replacement.

Fixes #4287

**How I verified it**

Relying on CI (vstest job in azure-pipelines.yml).

**Details if related**

Changed files:
- `tests/conftest.py`: `debian:jessie` → `debian:bookworm`
- `tests/test_mirror.py`: removed Jessie-era `skipif` guards on `test_MirrorToVlanAddRemove` and `test_MirrorDestMoveVlan`, removed unused `distro` and `StrictVersion` imports
